name: Yet Another Tournament
description: You are participating in Yet Another Tournament. There are $$$n + 1$$$ participants: you and $$$n$$$ other opponents, numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. Each two participants will play against each other exactly once. If the opponent $$$i$$$ plays against the opponent $$$j$$$, he wins if and only if $$$i \gt j$$$. When the opponent $$$i$$$ plays against you, everything becomes a little bit complicated. In order to get a win against opponent $$$i$$$, you need to prepare for the match for at least $$$a_i$$$ minutes — otherwise, you lose to that opponent. You have $$$m$$$ minutes in total to prepare for matches, but you can prepare for only one match at one moment. In other words, if you want to win against opponents $$$p_1, p_2, \dots, p_k$$$, you need to spend $$$a_{p_1} + a_{p_2} + \dots + a_{p_k}$$$ minutes for preparation — and if this number is greater than $$$m$$$, you cannot achieve a win against all of these opponents at the same time. The final place of each contestant is equal to the number of contestants with strictly more wins $$$+$$$ $$$1$$$. For example, if $$$3$$$ contestants have $$$5$$$ wins each, $$$1$$$ contestant has $$$3$$$ wins and $$$2$$$ contestants have $$$1$$$ win each, then the first $$$3$$$ participants will get the $$$1$$$-st place, the fourth one gets the $$$4$$$-th place and two last ones get the $$$5$$$-th place. Calculate the minimum possible place (lower is better) you can achieve if you can't prepare for the matches more than $$$m$$$ minutes in total.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 5 \cdot 10^5$$$; $$$0 \le m \le \sum\limits_{i=1}^{n}{a_i}$$$) — the number of your opponents and the total time you have for preparation. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \le a_i \le 1000$$$), where $$$a_i$$$ is the time you need to prepare in order to win against the $$$i$$$-th opponent. It's guaranteed that the total sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases doesn't exceed $$$5 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print the minimum possible place you can take if you can prepare for the matches no more than $$$m$$$ minutes in total.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1783C — Yet Another Tournament [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
